HPSA 'Proposed For Withdrawal' is often a handoff, not a loss. A re-designated area keeps its old HPSA_ID in that status while a new ID is marked Designated on the same census tracts. Adding the proposed population to the designated population counts people twice. Before calling an area at risk, join on HPSA_GEOGRAPHY_ID, or its first 9 digits so tract splits still match.
HPSA withdrawals come after replacement. 263 of 308 July 2026 withdrawals have tracts that are in a designated area today. 'Withdrawn' does not mean the tract lost shortage status.
An HPSA's DESIGNATION_DATE is the date of that ID, not of the area. MSSA 231/Porterville/Alpaugh shows 1992 on the proposed ID and 2025-10-22 on its replacement.

HPSA COMPONENT_NAME changes format by vintage: 'Census Tract X; County; California' on designated rows, 'Census Tract X, County, California' on proposed rows, a bare number on withdrawn rows. Match on HPSA_GEOGRAPHY_ID, never on COMPONENT_NAME.

Reported and predicted counts disagree about peaks. The US peak is Jun 2023 on reported counts but Aug 2023 on predicted. Hawaii's is Apr 2025 on reported but Aug 2023 on predicted. Pick one basis per claim, and use predicted for the newest months.

The newest month is the most under-reported in the file. The US Jan 2026 reported count is 1,252 below the predicted count. A peak-to-latest decline on reported counts is inflated, the same way a rise on reported counts is a floor.

Two VA tables give different age-adjusted rates for the same deaths. VA-user men: ALLCAUSE 48.5 and 53.4, SUICIDE_NATIONAL 47.69 and 53.04, with identical death counts (2,304 and 2,382). They use different age standards. Never compare a number from one table to a number from the other.

SUICIDE_NATIONAL's age-adjusted rate uses the US 2000 standard in 4 bands; I rebuilt it exactly. Ages 18-54 get 71% of the weight. For VA users, 67% of whom are 55 or older, the age-adjusted trend mostly describes the young minority. Check the age bands before claiming a trend.

In SUICIDE_NATIONAL, the 'Recent Veteran VHA User' and 'Other Veteran' age-band rows have no male or female split; every sex-specific column is null. Age-by-sex exists only for Veteran and Non-Veteran.

All-veteran suicide rates divide by VA's modeled veteran headcount, rounded to thousands, which fell 12% from 2018 to 2023. Veteran male suicides fell (6,445 to 6,091) while the rate rose. Always report the count beside the rate.

'Recent VHA user' is defined by using VA care in the year of death or the year before. That's circular selection: people in crisis who reach VA enter the group. Treat trends in this group as partly about who walks in the door.
